metadata.title: Git Commit Message Sources
metadata.description: Primary sources for Conventional Commits, Git hooks, commit linting, and release automation guidance.

standards.name: Conventional Commits Specification 1.0.0
standards.description: Authoritative conventional commit format and breaking-change rules. v1.0.0 is current stable as of July 2026; no v2 released.

standards.name: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
standards.description: Versioning rules commonly paired with Conventional Commits.

git_docs.name: Git Hooks
git_docs.description: Official source for hook behavior such as pre-commit, prepare-commit-msg, and commit-msg.

git_docs.name: Git Interpret Trailers
git_docs.description: Official trailer syntax for footers such as BREAKING CHANGE and issue references.

git_docs.name: How to Write a Git Commit Message

tooling.name: commitlint Getting Started
tooling.description: Official setup and config guidance. commitlint is at v21.x (21.2.1) as of July 2026, requires Node 22+; config uses ESM export default syntax.

tooling.name: semantic-release
tooling.description: Official automated release documentation driven by commit history. At v25.x and actively maintained as of mid-2026 (recent work adds npm trusted publishing).

tooling.name: Changesets Intro
tooling.description: Official changesets introduction for human-reviewed release notes in package repos.

tooling.name: Release Please Action
tooling.description: Official GitHub Action for PR-driven release automation. Reached v5 in April 2026 (Node 24 runtime); underlying release-please package is v17.x. Manifest/config-file approach remains preferred for multi-package repos. Re-verify the major tag before pinning — this project ships majors faster than most release tooling.

tooling.name: pre-commit Framework
tooling.description: Framework for managing repo hooks, including secret scanning and message validation wrappers.

tooling.name: standard-version
tooling.description: Deprecated since 2022 (not archived). README points adopters to release-please (GitHub-native) or the community fork commit-and-tag-version (non-GitHub CI). Do not adopt for new projects.

security.name: Gitleaks
security.description: Secret scanning for local repos and CI pipelines.

security.name: TruffleHog
security.description: Secret detection and verification in repositories and history.

security.name: CVSS v4.0 Calculator
security.description: Severity scoring reference for vulnerability-related commit notes and advisories.

ai_attribution.name: AI Commit Attribution Patterns 2026
ai_attribution.description: Emerging opt-in pattern: Assisted-by trailer in commit body for audit trail. Not a default requirement. Verified June 2026.

ai_attribution.name: Open Source AI Contributions: the Assisted-by Git Trailer Standard
ai_attribution.description: Assisted-by has converged as a distinct trailer from Co-Authored-By through 2026, adopted or discussed by Linux Kernel, Fedora, Rocky Linux, OpenTelemetry, Apache Software Foundation, LLVM, and QEMU. Rationale: Co-Authored-By implies authorship/copyright standing an AI tool cannot hold or sign a CLA for. Verified July 2026.

ai_attribution.name: Best Practices for Committing AI-Generated Code
ai_attribution.description: Industry guidance on quality review, attribution, and test coverage for AI-assisted commits.

optional_examples.name: JetBrains AI Assistant VCS Integration
optional_examples.description: Optional IDE-native commit message assistance example.

optional_examples.name: Windsurf AI Commit Messages
optional_examples.description: Optional IDE-native commit message assistance example.
